Structural axis KILLED with a mechanism, not enumeration: BB2_FINDREG_DEBUG proves the root flip is a global.c find_reg pass-0 scan for pseudo 86 (the D_8008EB40 table entry) whose exclusion sets are

Root re-located: the first-allocated allocno is pseudo 129 (div16), not 86, and its $v1 gap is a single regs_someone_prefers PREFERENCE bit (reachable from C) rather than a conflict bit (multiset-pinn

frontier.hypothesis: H9 - regs_someone_prefers[129]'s single $v1 bit is contributed by allocno 122 (abs_val), whose hard_reg_full_preferences is measured to be exactly {3}; removing that contribution seats div16 in $v1 and unwinds the whole cascade.
frontier.mechanism: prune_preferences (global.c:882-931) walks allocnos least-important-first and, for each higher-priority allocno i, unions hard_reg_full_preferences[j] over every lower-priority j with CONFLICTP(i,j). 122 is ord=1, exactly one step below 129 (ord=0), and is the only allocno in this function measured to carry a $v1 full-preference bit.
frontier.next_probe: PROVE the attribution before spending any C: run BB2_FINDREG_DEBUG over every allocno in the ord list to confirm 122 is the unique $v1-preferrer, and confirm CONFLICTP(129,122) by checking in the .lreg RTL whether abs_val's live range overlaps the *(s16 *)(arg0 + 0x1A) read. Only then attack 122's PREFERENCE (not its seat): locate the SET that pairs 122 with a $v1-seated local quantity and re-spell the abs/clamp block so that pairing does not form. Every candidate must measure at 159/159 - a form that changes the insn count is not a candidate.

frontier.hypothesis: H10 - the CONFLICTP prong is the cheaper half of H9: if div16's read is moved so its live range no longer overlaps abs_val's, 122 stops being a lower-priority CONFLICTING allocno of 129 and its $v1 preference never enters regs_someone_prefers[129], regardless of where that preference came from.
frontier.mechanism: prune_preferences only merges preferences across a CONFLICTP pair, so killing the overlap is equivalent to killing the preference for this purpose; live-range placement is exactly what structural statement re-association controls.
frontier.next_probe: Structural variants that move the *(s16 *)(arg0 + 0x1A) read relative to the abs/clamp block (above it, below the 0x14E store, into the arm that consumes it), each measured with sandbox at 159/159, with BB2_FINDREG_DEBUG=129 re-run on any variant that changes the score to read whether someone_prefers lost the 3.

frontier.hypothesis: H11 - the seat map's second half (sub_result, mflo temps, speed) follows for free once 129 is seated in $v1, because 129 is ord=0 and every other allocno is allocated after it.
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocates in a fixed priority order and each assignment ORs its hard reg into the conflicts of every conflicting allocno, so a change at ord=0 propagates through the whole subsequent scan.
frontier.next_probe: Do NOT assume it (s1's identical 'follows for free' claim about 86 is still unmeasured and s2's kills made it less likely). Once any form seats 129 in $v1, immediately re-run BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG=1 and the 159-line aligned diff and record which seats actually followed and which did not.
